ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a large equilateral triangle, and the total length of each of the three sides is 5. Each side is divided into three segments labeled 1, 3, 1; the gray shading is in the middle, and the uncolored parts are exactly the small triangles at the three corners: one at the top, one at the lower left corner, and one at the lower right corner. Then reason: The side length of each uncolored corner triangle is 1, and they are all similar to the large equilateral triangle with side length 5. The area ratio of similar figures is equal to the square of the side length ratio, so each small triangle occupies (1/5)^2=1/25 of the area of the large triangle. The three uncolored small triangles together occupy 3/25=12%. Therefore the shaded part occupies 100%-12%=88%.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as an equilateral triangle of side 5, with each side split into labeled lengths 1, 3, and 1. The shaded region is the large triangle with exactly three unshaded corner triangles removed: the top triangle, the bottom-left triangle, and the bottom-right triangle. Each unshaded corner triangle has side length 1 and is similar to the large equilateral triangle of side 5. Compute the total unshaded area fraction as 3*(1/5)^2 = 3/25 = 12%, so the shaded percentage is 100% - 12% = 88%.
